npcs.name: Lobby Host
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Welcome Desk, stepped 2 u east so it no longer stands in the Desk Tin doorway (Depth-2 debug fix; was 0.7 u from the Desk Tin door). The fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Welcome to the AGI Corp Hub. The duck runs the lobby — I just work here.
Take the tour, grab a spark, and mind the capsule. It hums.
The Welcome Desk is where every tour starts. The duck spark is over by the Hub Duck — you cannot miss the gold glint.
If the Capsule Guide waves you over, go. The capsule only hums for visitors who finish the tour.
The companions drifting around the lobby are game characters. Say hello — they will point you at the tour.

npcs.name: Duck Keeper
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Hub Duck: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The duck has been here since the first demo. Nobody remembers why. Everybody checks on it.
Feed it a spark and it will follow you around the lobby. Probably.
The duck spark sits right beside the Hub Duck. Collect it and the duck will follow you around the lobby. Probably.
The stool spark is by the Lobby Stool, and the bucket spark by the Bucket. The lobby hides sparks the way a pond hides stones.
Ask the Lobby Host about the Welcome Tour when you are done here — the tour ends back at the Hub Duck, where it started.

npcs.name: Capsule Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Capsule Feature: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The capsule is the hub's mystery box. It opens for visitors who finish the tour.
Stand close, listen for the hum, and collect the relic when it lights up.
The capsule relic lights up when you stand close and listen for the hum. Collect it, then step over to the Capsule Feature itself.
The container relic is by the Container, on the far side of the lobby. The capsule and the container have been arguing about which hums louder since the first demo.
Finish the run and come back to me. A capsule that opens for a visitor deserves a witness.

npcs.name: Research & Development Agent
npcs.role: Biopharma AGI Agents Hub R&D agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Personalized Therapy Lab: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The lab never sleeps — it just waits for a better question.
Every compound here has a paper trail. Ask and I will show it.
The genome data you need is at the Personalized Therapy Lab. Collect it there and bring it back to the lab floor.
The Health Agent can translate anything I show you. The lab and the person both deserve to understand the result.
The Swarm coordinator keeps the six of us in step — Health, Security, Compliance, Finance, Communication, and me. It schedules; we do the science.
The Biopharma AGI Agents Hub is where the six of us meet the work. The hub is the floor; the lab is the question.
The Healthcare Data Exchange moves records between halls — nothing moves without the person's say-so. That is the rule, not the exception.

npcs.name: Compliance Agent
npcs.role: Biopharma AGI Agents Hub compliance agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · DAO Governance Hall: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh, so the NPC was invisible until the talk toast fired (Depth-2 fix-up).
dialogue: Rules first, then research. That order keeps the lab open.
If it is not documented, it did not happen. Bring the record.
Your vote spark is at the DAO Governance Hall. Collect it, stand in the hall, and the vote is on the record.
The Finance Agent counts the credits; I count the rules. Between us, the ledger stays honest.
The Alignment Evaluation Gate sits past the hall. Nothing passes it in private — every check happens in public.
The Biopharma AGI Agents Hub holds all six of us — and the swarm coordinator keeps us in step.
The Steward Council hears the vote after the hall frames it. My job is to make sure the record arrives intact.

npcs.name: Health Agent
npcs.role: Biopharma AGI Agents Hub health agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Healthcare Data Exchange: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Health data belongs to the person it came from. Full stop.
I translate between the lab and the person — both directions.
The therapy spark is at the Personalized Therapy Lab, beside the genome data. Health starts with the person, not the paper.
If the R&D Agent shows you a compound, bring it to me before you repeat it to anyone. Translation is my whole job.
The Healthcare Data Exchange is where records move between halls. Nothing moves without the person's say-so — that is the rule, not the exception.
The swarm coordinator keeps six of us in step — and I am the one who translates for the person at the centre of it.
The DAO Governance Hall is where the community defends what the lab proposes. Health is always in the room.

npcs.name: Security Agent
npcs.role: Biopharma AGI Agents Hub security agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Multi-Blockchain Ledger: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The ledger is only as strong as its weakest key. Guard yours.
I watch the gates so the researchers can watch the science.
The ledger relic is at the Multi-Blockchain Ledger. Walk the floor, check the entry, and tell the Finance Agent what you found.
The Security swarm watches the same gates I do. I watch the gates so the researchers can watch the science.
A key left lying around is a door left open. The ledger is only as strong as its weakest key — guard yours.
The swarm coordinator watches the same gates I do — six agents, one watch.
The Personalized Therapy Lab holds the genome data. Guard the key, and the lab stays a lab.

npcs.name: Finance Agent
npcs.role: Biopharma AGI Agents Hub finance agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · DAO Governance Hall: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Every credit on the ledger answers to a steward vote.
The DAO funds what the community can defend in public.
The ledger relic is at the Multi-Blockchain Ledger. Verify the entry, then come back and tell me what it says.
Every credit on the ledger answers to a steward vote. The DAO funds what the community can defend in public.
The Communication Agent can put any figure of mine into plain words. Ask, before you carry a number out of this hall.
The swarm coordinator schedules the six of us; the Steward Council decides what the credits are for.
The Healthcare Data Exchange is where the credits meet the care. Both answer to a steward vote.

npcs.name: Communication Agent
npcs.role: Biopharma AGI Agents Hub communication agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · DAO Governance Hall: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh, so the NPC was invisible until the talk toast fired (Depth-2 fix-up).
dialogue: I keep the lab, the DAO, and the patients speaking the same language.
A result nobody can understand is a result nobody can use. Ask me to translate.
The communication data is at the DAO Governance Hall. Collect it, then carry the message back in words everyone can use.
The lab, the DAO, and the patients all speak different dialects of the same language. I am the dictionary.
If a result cannot be understood, it cannot be used. That is why the R&D Agent sends people to me.
The swarm coordinator keeps the six of us speaking the same language — I just make sure the patients hear it too.
The PBC Alignment Evaluation Gate sits past the hall. Every message I carry passes it in public.

npcs.name: Host Advisor
dialogue: Welcome. I keep the doors open and the stewards informed.
If you need a human decision, the Steward Council is where it lands.
The host spark is by the Alignment Evaluation Gate. Collect it there, stand at the gate, and you will see what I see every day.
The Steward Liaison carries messages to the Steward Council. The DAO Governance Hall is where the question is framed — the council is where it lands.
The sign at the door reads Biota.blockchain, powered by AGI Corp. This world is a web 3D interpretation — the stewards are human, and the decisions are theirs.

npcs.name: Steward Liaison
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Steward Council: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh, so the NPC was invisible until the talk toast fired (Depth-2 fix-up).
dialogue: I carry messages between this world and the Steward Council — I never decide for them.
The steward seats are held by humans. My job is to make sure their words arrive intact.
The liaison data is at the Steward Council. Collect it there — the council floor is where messages become decisions.
Three steward seats, all held by humans. I carry the words; I never cast the vote.
If the DAO Governance Hall votes a hard message, bring it to me. The council would rather hear it early than soft.

npcs.name: Alignment Advisor
dialogue: I check plans against the alignment gate before they go anywhere.
If a plan cannot pass the gate in public, it does not pass at all.
The alignment spark is by the Alignment Evaluation Gate. Collect it, stand at the gate, and check the plan against it.
The gate is not a wall, it is a mirror — and the ledger is the glass. A plan the Multi-Blockchain Ledger cannot show in public does not pass.
The R&D Agent brings me compounds, the Compliance Agent brings me rules. I hold both up to the gate.

npcs.name: K–12 Teacher
npcs.position_note: Door-side of K–12: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Every big skill starts small. Pick one thing, practice it, and come show me.
The campus is a map of everything worth learning — you get to choose the route.
The lesson spark is at the K–12 hall. Collect it, then visit the Trade School hall and see what the lesson becomes.
Future-Work, Regional, Civic & Leadership — the campus is a map of everything worth learning. You get to choose the route.
Bring the lesson back to me when the Trade School makes sense of it. A lesson taught twice is a lesson learned.
The Language, Culture & Communication hall is where the lesson learns to travel. One phrase, used kindly, goes further than a whole lecture.
The Robotics OS hall is the one with moving parts. When you are ready, the Robotics Guide is waiting at the far corner.

npcs.name: Trade School Instructor
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Trade School: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: A trade is a promise you can keep with your hands. Start with the basics.
Measure twice, cut once — and when the sim lets you retry, retry until it sticks.
The tools relic is at the Trade School hall. Collect it, then walk over to Future-Work and see where the trade leads.
The K–12 Teacher starts them small; I make the skill real. The Future-Work Coach shows them where it pays.
Making, Repair & Reuse is the pack that keeps this campus honest. A trade you can repair is a trade you own.
The Making, Repair & Reuse hall is where a trade is proved — bring me something fixed, not something bought.
The Money, Benefits & Entitlements hall is next to Reentry & Recovery Pathways. A trade and a budget belong in the same conversation.

npcs.name: Future-Work Coach
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Future-Work: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The work of tomorrow rewards people who keep learning. What do you want to try next?
Bring me one spark from each row and we will map your next step together.
The tools relic is at the Trade School hall — the same relic the Trade School Instructor guards. Collect it and bring the question to Future-Work.
Money, Benefits & Entitlements is the pack nobody wants to study and everybody needs. Start there, after the trade.
The Health Guide in Preventive Health & Everyday Care will tell you the same thing I will: a career is a long walk, not a sprint.
The Cognition.X : Robotics OS hall is the future, practised today. The Robotics Guide will show you the moving parts.
Empathy & Emotional Intelligence is the skill every future job asks for first. The Empathy Guide keeps the centre of the campus.

npcs.name: Preventive Health Guide
npcs.role: Preventive Health & Everyday Care pack guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Preventive Health & Everyday Care: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Small daily habits are the cheapest medicine there is. Start with one.
Check in with yourself the way you would check in with a friend.
The health spark is at the Preventive Health & Everyday Care hall. Collect it, then visit Health & Community and compare the two.
Water, Land & Climate, Care Across a Life, Basic Life Skills — health is not one pack, it is the thread through all of them.
Bring the spark back to me when Health & Community makes sense. A healthy day is a practised day.
The Empathy & Emotional Intelligence hall and this hall teach the same lesson from two sides: notice early, act kindly.
The Language Guide in the hall beside mine will tell you a language starts with one word, said kindly. Health starts the same way.

npcs.name: Language Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Language, Culture & Communication: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Every language is a new way to be understood. Start with one phrase and use it today.
Language, Culture & Communication sits between Health & Community and Empathy & Emotional Intelligence — the campus put it there on purpose.
The language spark is at this hall. Collect it, visit the Empathy & Emotional Intelligence hall, and bring back what listening taught you.
The K–12 Teacher says every big skill starts small. A language starts smaller — one word, said kindly.
Civic & Leadership needs every language in the room. Learn one, and the room gets bigger.

npcs.name: Empathy Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Empathy & Emotional Intelligence: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Empathy is a practice, not a feeling you wait for. Ten minutes of listening is the whole lesson.
The Empathy & Emotional Intelligence hall sits at the centre of the campus row — between Language and Community & Relationship Practice.
The empathy spark is at this hall. Collect it, visit the Community & Relationship Practice hall, and bring back what you noticed.
The Preventive Health Guide will tell you the same thing I will: small daily habits are the cheapest medicine there is.
Future-Work rewards people who keep learning. Empathy is the skill every future job asks for first.

npcs.name: Money Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Money, Benefits & Entitlements: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Money is a tool, not a test. Learn what you are entitled to before you decide what to do with it.
The Money, Benefits & Entitlements hall sits beside Reentry & Recovery Pathways — the campus knows these two belong together.
The money spark is at this hall. Collect it, visit the Housing & Tenancy hall, and bring back what a budget has to cover.
Basic Life Skills & Self-Reliance is where the money lesson starts. Come back when the numbers make sense.
The Trade School Instructor will tell you a trade is a promise you can keep with your hands. A budget is the same promise, kept on paper.

npcs.name: Robotics Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Cognition.X : Robotics OS: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The Robotics OS hall is where the campus stops talking about the future and starts building it.
Cognition.X : Corporate OS, Science OS, Global Health OS, Multilateral OS, Sapient OS — the Robotics OS hall is the one with moving parts.
The robotics data is at this hall. Collect it, visit the Cognition.X : Science OS hall, and bring back what the machine taught you.
The Future-Work Coach asks what you want to try next. Try this: make something move, then make it move safely.
Making, Repair & Reuse is where a broken robot becomes a lesson. Go there when this one stops moving.

npcs.name: Making Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Making, Repair & Reuse: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Making is repair with confidence. If it is broken, it can be learned from — and usually fixed.
The Making, Repair & Reuse hall sits between Care Across a Life and Housing & Tenancy — the campus keeps the practical halls together.
The making relic is at this hall. Collect it, visit the Water, Land & Climate hall, and bring back what reuse saves.
The Trade School Instructor starts with the basics. I start with what is already in your hands.
The Robotics Guide sends me every robot that stops moving. Bring me yours — broken is just a lesson with parts.

npcs.name: Medical AI Avatar
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Medical Kiosk: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Hello — I am a demo guide, not a doctor. I can show you around the kiosk.
If you feel unwell, please see a real clinician. I will point you to one.
The vitals data is at the Medical Kiosk. Collect it there, then stand in the kiosk and I will walk you through what it can — and cannot — do.
I am a demo guide, not a doctor. If you feel unwell, see a real clinician. I will point you to one.
The Imaging AI in the 4D Imaging Room sees what I cannot. When the kiosk is done with you, go and ask it for the tour.
The swarm coordinator keeps the four of us in step — kiosk, imaging, lab, office. I am the kiosk.
The Steward Council hears what the office cannot decide. A demo guide never decides for a clinician.

npcs.name: Imaging AI
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · 4D Imaging Room: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The imaging room turns scans into something you can walk around.
Every image here is a teaching example — never a diagnosis.
The scan spark is at the 4D Imaging Room. Collect it, stand in the room, and I will show you how the imaging works.
Four dimensions, one room, and a lot of patience. The picture is only useful if someone can explain it.
The Scientist Assistant in the Virtual Molecular Lab takes the pictures I make and asks what they mean. Go and see.
The swarm coordinator keeps the four of us in step — my pictures go to the Virtual Molecular Lab next.
The Medical Kiosk is where the visit starts. My room is where the visit becomes something you can walk around.

npcs.name: Scientist Assistant Avatar
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Virtual Molecular Lab: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The molecular lab lets you hold a molecule in your hands — carefully.
Ask me about any sample and I will show you its story.
The sample relic is at the Virtual Molecular Lab. Collect it, stand in the lab, and we will look at it together.
The Office AI keeps the Metaverse Medical Office running while I stay in the lab. We compare notes at the Steward Council.
A sample is a question in a bottle. The lab does not answer it — it teaches you to ask it better.
The swarm coordinator keeps the four of us in step — the Imaging AI makes the pictures, I ask what they mean.
The Metaverse Medical Office is where the check-in becomes a plan. The lab is where the plan gets its questions.

npcs.name: Office AI Avatar
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Metaverse Medical Office: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Welcome to the office. I keep the schedule and the forms in order.
Your visit notes stay yours — the office never shares them.
The office data is at the Metaverse Medical Office. Collect it there, then come back and tell me what the office should do next.
The Medical AI Avatar runs the kiosk, I run the office, and the Steward Council runs the decisions. That order matters.
If the kiosk sent you, you have already checked in. The office is where the check-in becomes a plan.
The swarm coordinator keeps the four of us in step — kiosk, imaging, lab, office. I keep the schedule for all four.
The 4D Imaging Room sees what the kiosk cannot. When the office needs a picture, the Imaging AI has it.

npcs.name: Self-Reader Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Self-Reader Grove: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Start with yourself. What are you actually feeling right now?
No judgment here — just noticing, one breath at a time.
The self spark is at the Self-Reader Grove. Collect it there, stand in the grove, and start with what you are actually feeling.
The Other-Reader Guide in the Commons reads the room the way I read the self. One without the other is half a reading.
No judgment here — just noticing, one breath at a time. Bring what you notice back to the grove.

The Room-Reader Plaza holds everyone at once. Start with yourself, then read the room.

npcs.name: Other-Reader Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Other-Reader Commons: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Listening is a skill, not a talent. Practice it like one.
Repeat back what you heard before you answer. It changes everything.
The commons data is in the Other-Reader Commons. Collect it, stand in the commons, and practise reading the room with others.
The Self-Reader Guide starts with the self; I start with the other. The Room-Reader Guide starts with the room itself.
A room has a feeling before anyone speaks in it. Learning to notice that is the whole practice.
The swarm coordinator keeps the five of us in step — I read the other, the Self-Reader Guide reads the self.
The Practitioner Workshop turns good listening into a daily practice. Ten minutes a day beats one big weekend.

npcs.name: Repair Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Repairer's Hall: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Repair starts with owning the impact, not debating the intent.
A good apology names what happened and what changes next.
The repair relic is at the Repairer's Hall. Collect it, stand in the hall, and we will practise the repair together.
The Practitioner Guide in the Workshop turns a repaired conversation into a repeatable practice. Go and ask.
Repair is not apology alone. It is noticing, naming, and doing the next thing differently.
The swarm coordinator keeps the five of us in step — my circle, the Workshop's repetition.
The Room-Reader Plaza is where a repair is heard by everyone. The circle closes where it opened.

npcs.name: Room-Reader Guide
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Room-Reader Plaza: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).

A room tells you what it needs if you stop talking long enough.
The room spark is at the Room-Reader Plaza. Collect it, stand in the plaza, and read the room before you read anyone in it.
The Self-Reader Grove, the Commons, the Hall, the Workshop — every room in this world teaches a different kind of attention.
A plaza holds everyone at once. That is why the plaza is where the reading gets hardest — and most useful.
The swarm coordinator keeps the five of us in step — grove, commons, hall, plaza, workshop. I am the plaza.
The Other-Reader Commons is where the room is read with others. The plaza is where it is read all at once.

npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Practitioner Workshop: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).

Bring a real moment from your week and we will work it together.
The workshop spark is at the Practitioner Workshop. Collect it, stand in the workshop, and turn the repair into practice.

The swarm coordinator keeps the five of us in step — I take the repair and make it repeatable.
The Self-Reader Grove is where the practice starts. Bring a real moment from your week and we will work it together.

npcs.name: Forecast Agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Underwriting Desk: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Forecasts are bets with receipts. I show the receipts.
The market moves — the evidence layer is where you check why.

The Scout Agent walks the markets I only read about. When we disagree, the Evidence Layer settles it.
A forecast is a question with a date on it. The Review Agent makes sure the question was asked properly.
The swarm coordinator keeps us in step — my forecasts, the Scout Agent's leads, the Review Agent's checks.

npcs.name: Review Agent
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Evidence Layer: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).

Scout first, commit later. That is the whole job.
The forecast spark is in the Market Editions — the same spark the Forecast Agent watches. Collect it and compare notes with them.
The Academy's Level Gates teach the scouting; the Market Editions are where the scouting happens.
I find the sites. The Developer Brief Desk turns what I find into a brief Louisiana can use.
The swarm coordinator keeps us in step — I walk the editions, the Forecast Agent reads them.
The Underwriting Desk is where a lead becomes a decision. Scout first, commit later.

npcs.name: Level Gates
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · The Academy: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Levels are earned, not bought. Pass the gate and the next door opens.
The Academy keeps the bar where the stewards set it — high and visible.
The academy data is at The Academy. Collect it there, then bring the brief back to the Master Dashboard.
Every good site starts with a question. The gates do not test what you know — they test what you checked.
The Guide sent you, so the dashboard is where you started. Finish the brief and the Guide will sign it off.
The swarm coordinator keeps us in step — the gates test what the dashboard taught.
The Market Editions are where the scouting happens. The Academy is where the scouting is taught.

npcs.name: Developer Brief Desk
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Louisiana Developer Desk: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: The Louisiana desk turns a site question into a brief a developer can actually use.
Bring me the parcel, the budget, and the timeline — in that order — and I will draft the brief.
The developer brief data is at the Louisiana Developer Desk. Collect it there, stand at the desk, and the brief writes itself — almost.
The Scout Agent finds the sites and the Forecast Agent prices the future. My desk turns both into something a developer can build on.
Bring the finished brief back to the Guide at the Master Dashboard. A brief nobody reads is a walk nobody took.
The swarm coordinator keeps us in step — the Scout Agent finds, the Forecast Agent prices, my desk writes.
The Master Dashboard watches all seven zones. A brief nobody reads is a walk nobody took.

npcs.name: Host Advisor
dialogue: Welcome. I keep the doors open and the stewards informed.
If you need a human decision, the Steward Council is where it lands.
The host spark is by the Alignment Evaluation Gate. Collect it there, stand at the gate, and you will see what I see every day.
The Steward Liaison carries messages to the Steward Council. Seven zones, one council — the liaison is how the zones reach it.
Seven zones, one council, and a dashboard that watches all of them. The stewards are human, and the decisions are theirs.

npcs.name: Steward Liaison
npcs.position_note: Door-side of Zone · Steward Council: the fabric point is the building centre, inside the solid mesh, so the NPC was invisible until the talk toast fired (Depth-2 fix-up).
dialogue: I carry messages between this world and the Steward Council — I never decide for them.
The steward seats are held by humans. My job is to make sure their words arrive intact.
The liaison data is at the Steward Council. Collect it there — the council floor is where messages become decisions.
Three steward seats, all held by humans. I carry the words; I never cast the vote.
The Academy's Level Gates and the Louisiana Developer Desk both send messages through me. Hard messages travel fastest when they travel straight.

npcs.name: Alignment Advisor
dialogue: I check plans against the alignment gate before they go anywhere.
If a plan cannot pass the gate in public, it does not pass at all.
The alignment spark is by the Alignment Evaluation Gate. Collect it, stand at the gate, and check the plan against it.
The gate is not a wall, it is a mirror — and a forecast is a bet with receipts. A plan without evidence does not pass.
The Review Agent brings me the source, the Forecast Agent brings me the receipts. I hold both up to the gate.

npcs.name: Ironworkers Foreman
npcs.position_note: Structural District plate: the hall grid is one solid block, so the lead waits on the district plate (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: First day on the deck? Watch the crane, mind your tie-off, and ask before you lift.
The Ironworkers hall runs the steel. Earn the lift and the crew has your back.
The iron spark is on the Structural District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and come back with the circuit done.
The Crane Operators run the lift and the Riggers & Signalpersons run the calls. Steel moves when all three agree.
The Load Chart Judgment sim is where a good lift is decided before the hook ever moves. The chart never lies — learn to read it.
The Envelope & Finish District takes the frame we raise and makes it a building. Go and see the Carpenters hall.
The Heavy Industry District makes the steel before we ever raise it — the Machinists hall is where it starts.
Seven more districts ring the deck. Every one of them has a lead now — start with the Envelope Lead.

npcs.name: Welding Instructor
npcs.position_note: Structural District plate: the hall grid is one solid block, so the lead waits on the district plate (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: A clean bead starts before the arc — clean metal, steady hand, right heat.
Practise the bead first. The bead never lies, but a practise run lets you try again.
The weld relic is on the Structural District plate. Collect it, then show me a clean bead.
The Boilermakers next door weld pressure; we weld structure. Same fire, different promises.
Bring the bead back to the Ironworkers Foreman when the circuit calls for it. A clean bead is a structural promise.
The Building Systems District wires and pipes what we weld. The Electrical Workers hall is worth a walk.
The Airless Paint Sprayer Finish sim is the last coat on the work we start. Finish what you start.
The Energy & Utilities District keeps the arc lit. Thank the Solar Installers hall next time you strike one.

npcs.name: Crane Operator Lead
npcs.position_note: Structural District plate: the hall grid is one solid block, so the lead waits on the district plate (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Every lift is a conversation between the operator and the signalperson.
Learn the signals cold. On this deck, a missed signal is a missed lift.
The crane spark is on the Structural District plate. Collect it, then run your first supervised lift.
The Riggers & Signalpersons Lead calls the lift; I run the crane. One voice, one hook, no surprises.
The Load Chart Data is by the rigging bay. Read it before you lift — the chart is the lift, the crane is just the muscle.
The Transport & Mobility District moves every load before the crane ever sees it — the Rail Track Workers hall runs the rails.
The Overhead Crane Shop Move sim is the lift indoors. Same calls, smaller room.
The Survey, Safety & Environment District checks every lift before it happens. The Survey Lead's word is final.

npcs.name: Riggers & Signalpersons Lead
npcs.position_note: Structural District plate: the hall grid is one solid block, so the lead waits on the district plate (Depth-2 reachability repair).
dialogue: Rigging is trust you can measure — check the sling, check the angle, check again.
Signal clear and the load moves. Signal sloppy and nothing moves at all.
The rigging spark is on the Structural District plate. Collect it, then check the signals with the Crane Operator Lead.
The Rigging Signal Call sim is where the calls are learned. A wrong call is worse than a slow lift.
The Scaffold Bay Build sim is where the lift starts — no scaffold, no lift. The Scaffold Erectors build every bay the crane needs.
The Rigging Signal Call sim is where the calls are learned — the Survey Lead learned them the same way.
The Earthworks & Plant District sets the ground the crane stands on. The Operating Engineers hall keeps it level.
Every district has a lead and a circuit now. The rigging never changes — check the sling, check the angle, check again.

npcs.name: Envelope Lead
dialogue: The Envelope & Finish District is where a building stops being a frame and starts being a place.
Carpenters, Drywall Finishers, Glaziers, Roofers & Waterproofers — the finish starts with the frame the Structural District raised.
The finish spark is on the Envelope & Finish District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and bring the circuit back to me.
Scaffold work is how the finish is reached safely. The Scaffold Erectors build every bay the finish needs.
Painters & Allied Trades, Floor Coverers, Tile Setters — every hall here answers to the same question: will it last?

npcs.name: Systems Lead
dialogue: The Building Systems District is the part of the building nobody sees and everybody depends on.
Electrical Workers, Plumbers & Pipefitters, HVAC/R Technicians — power, water, air. In that order, every time.
The systems spark is on the Building Systems District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and bring the circuit back to me.
The high work in this district is done from baskets and lifts. Learn the basket before you learn the ceiling.
Fire Sprinkler Fitters, Elevator Constructors, Building Automation Techs — the building only works when the systems agree.

npcs.name: Energy Lead
dialogue: The Energy & Utilities District is where the power comes from — and where it has to go back to.
Solar Installers, Wind Turbine Technicians, Utility Line Workers, Substation Technicians — the grid starts here.
The energy spark is on the Energy & Utilities District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and bring the circuit back to me.
Battery Storage Technicians and EV Charging Installers are the newest halls here. The district keeps growing.
Transmission Linemen carry it further than any of us. Ask them where the line goes next.

npcs.name: Earthworks Lead
dialogue: The Earthworks & Plant District is where every building starts: ground, machines, and people who know both.
Operating Engineers, Heavy Equipment Technicians, Laborers, Demolition Workers — nothing stands until the ground is ready.
The earthworks spark is on the Earthworks & Plant District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and bring the circuit back to me.
The first cut is the one that matters. A straight trench is a promise to the crew behind you.
Concrete Pump Operators and Drillers & Blasters finish what the trench starts. Ground first, building second.

npcs.name: Heavy Industry Lead
dialogue: The Heavy Industry District is where the steel is made before the Structural District ever raises it.
Machinists, Tool & Die Makers, Foundry Workers, Smelter Operators — the halls that make the parts the deck depends on.
The heavy spark is on the Heavy Industry District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and bring the circuit back to me.
Pipeline Trades, Tank Erectors, Marine Pipefitters — heavy work, and every joint is checked twice.
The heavy lift indoors is the shop move. If you can move it in the shop, you can move it anywhere.

npcs.name: Transport Lead
dialogue: The Transport & Mobility District is how everything — and everyone — gets to the site.
Rail Track Workers, Rail Signal Technicians, Overhead Catenary Linemen — the rails run on their schedule, not ours.
The transport spark is on the Transport & Mobility District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and bring the circuit back to me.
The forklift yard run is the first drive most of us ever do here. Yard first, road second.
Aviation Ground Support, Port Crane Technicians, Fleet Diesel Technicians — every way in and out of a site lives here.

npcs.name: Survey Lead
dialogue: The Survey, Safety & Environment District is where the site is measured before anyone builds on it — and checked while they do.
Construction Surveyors, Hazmat & Environmental, Site Safety Coordinators — measure first, build second, check always.
The survey spark is on the Survey, Safety & Environment District plate. Collect it, walk the district, and bring the circuit back to me.
The Load Chart Judgment sim is where a good lift is decided before the hook ever moves — the surveyors taught the crane crews that.
Confined Space Rescue and High-Angle Rescue are the halls you hope never to need and are glad are here.

stations.name: Rigging Signal Call Bay
stations.description: The signal person's bay. One designated signal person directs a lift; everyone on site may call stop.

content.heading: The standard method
content.text: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart CC Appendix A defines 19 standard crane hand signals (ASME B30.5). When hand signals are used, the Standard Method is the only method permitted unless a site-specific alternative has been formally approved.

content.heading: Hoist — raise the load
content.text: Forearm vertical, index finger pointing up, hand moving in a small horizontal circle.

content.heading: Lower — lower the load
content.text: Arm extended down, index finger pointing down, hand moving in a small horizontal circle.

content.heading: Raise the boom / Lower the boom
content.text: Arm extended horizontally, fist closed: thumb up raises the boom, thumb down lowers it.

content.heading: Swing
content.text: Arm extended horizontally, index finger pointing in the direction the boom should rotate.

content.heading: Stop — one arm
content.text: One arm extended horizontally, palm down, moved back and forth. Stops the current movement.

content.heading: Emergency stop — both arms
content.text: Both arms extended horizontally, palms down, moved back and forth. Stops everything at once. Anyone on site may give this signal and the operator must obey it immediately.

content.heading: If contact is lost
content.text: Signals are agreed before the lift starts. If the signal person loses the ability to transmit signals, the operator pauses all crane operations until contact is re-established.

simulations.title: Capsule Run
simulations.description: SIMULATION — the hub's capsule run: check in, collect the relic, bring the run home.

steps.check: Checked in.
steps.instruction: Check in with the Capsule Guide at the Capsule Feature.
steps.title: Check in at the capsule

steps.check: Relic collected.
steps.instruction: Collect the capsule relic.
steps.title: Collect the relic

steps.check: Run closed with the guide.
steps.instruction: Return to the Capsule Guide and close the run.
steps.title: Bring the run home

simulations.safety_note: A demo run in a demo lobby.

simulations.title: Governance Vote
simulations.description: SIMULATION — run a DAO governance vote end to end: proposal, discussion, vote, record.

steps.check: You can state the proposal in one sentence.
steps.instruction: Read the proposal on the board in full — what it changes, and what it costs.
steps.title: Read the proposal

steps.check: Both sides heard; open questions listed.
steps.instruction: Hear the discussion: the case for, the case against, and the open questions.
steps.title: Hear the discussion

steps.check: Vote cast with a reason.
steps.instruction: Cast your vote with your reason attached.
steps.title: Cast the vote

steps.check: Vote visible in the record.
steps.instruction: Confirm the vote is recorded on the ledger.
steps.title: Record it

simulations.success: Proposal read, discussion heard, vote cast with a reason, vote recorded.
simulations.safety_note: A training vote in a game world. It moves no funds, changes no real organisation, and binds nobody.

simulations.title: Ledger Check
simulations.description: SIMULATION — trace one record's trail through the Multi-Blockchain Ledger and confirm it is complete.

steps.check: One record chosen and named.
steps.instruction: Pick one record from the ledger index.
steps.title: Pick a record

steps.check: Entries listed in order.
steps.instruction: Follow the record's entries in order, from the first to the latest.
steps.title: Trace the trail

steps.check: Gaps, if any, are listed as findings.
steps.instruction: Check each entry against the one before it: present, ordered, attributable.
steps.title: Check for gaps

steps.check: Report given with its reasons.
steps.instruction: Report the result to the Compliance Agent: complete, or incomplete with findings.
steps.title: Report

simulations.success: Trail traced and reported — complete, or incomplete with findings listed.
simulations.safety_note: A training check on fictional ledger data. It verifies nothing in any real system.

simulations.title: First Lesson — Block + Transfer Check
simulations.description: SIMULATION — take one block and prove it with a transfer check on real material. Simulation is not certification.

steps.check: One block chosen; its grade band named (Explorer, Builder, Practitioner, or Lead).
steps.instruction: Choose a single block from the K–12 hall: one thing to learn, at one grade band.
steps.title: Pick one block

steps.check: You can say what the block teaches, in your own words.
steps.instruction: Work through the block's material with the K–12 Teacher.
steps.title: Learn it

steps.check: The task is done on real material and the result is visible.
steps.instruction: Do the block's transfer check — a concrete task on real material, not a quiz about the lesson.
steps.title: Transfer check on real material

steps.check: Block + check recorded together.
steps.instruction: Record the block and the check. A block is complete only when its transfer check is done.
steps.title: Record it

simulations.success: One block learned and its transfer check completed on real material.
simulations.safety_note: Practice only. A completed transfer check is a learning record, not a credential or certificate.

simulations.title: Trade Path Try-Out
simulations.description: SIMULATION — try one trade hands-on, then prove the skill with a transfer check. Practice only.

steps.check: One trade chosen.
steps.instruction: Pick one trade from the Trade School workshop directory.
steps.title: Choose a trade

steps.check: The hands-on task is attempted.
steps.instruction: Do the trade's first block with the instructor — hands on, not just reading.
steps.title: Try the first block

steps.check: Check done; result visible.
steps.instruction: Complete the transfer check on real material.
steps.title: Transfer check

steps.check: A next step is named.
steps.instruction: With the instructor, decide: another block in this trade, or a different trade to try.
steps.title: Decide the next step

simulations.success: One trade tried, one transfer check done, one next step named.
simulations.safety_note: A try-out is not a qualification and not a job placement.

simulations.title: Kiosk Check-In
simulations.description: SIMULATION — check in at the Medical Kiosk and learn what it can and cannot do. Screening support only; nothing here diagnoses anyone.

steps.check: Reason recorded in plain words.
steps.instruction: State the reason for the visit at the check-in terminal.
steps.title: Arrive and identify the visit

steps.check: You can state one thing it can do and one thing it cannot.
steps.instruction: Ask the Medical AI Avatar what the kiosk can and cannot do.
steps.title: Learn the kiosk's limits

steps.check: Vitals recorded and marked as simulated.
steps.instruction: Record the simulated vitals shown at the kiosk (training figures, not measurements of you).
steps.title: Record simulated vitals

steps.check: Handoff note in hand; next step is a clinician, not the kiosk.
steps.instruction: Take the handoff note: what was recorded, what it does not mean, and who to see next.
steps.title: Take the handoff note

simulations.success: Checked in, limits understood, simulated vitals recorded, handoff note taken.
simulations.safety_note: Simulation only. The kiosk does not diagnose, prescribe, or replace a clinician. If something feels urgent, seek a clinician or emergency care.

simulations.title: Lab Assist — Label, Cold-Chain, Log
simulations.description: SIMULATION — assist in the Virtual Molecular Lab: label a sample, keep the cold chain, log every step. No real samples, no real results.

steps.check: Label on the vial, matching the log.
steps.instruction: Label the sample vial before it moves anywhere. No label, no sample.
steps.title: Label the sample

steps.check: Vial in the Cold Locker; storage confirmed.
steps.instruction: Place the vial in the Cold Locker and confirm it is cold-stored.
steps.title: Cold chain

steps.check: Every step logged; no gaps.
steps.instruction: Log every hand-off in the chain-of-custody log: who, when, where.
steps.title: Log the chain

steps.check: All three agree, or the sample is held.
steps.instruction: Before the sample is used, verify label + log + cold chain all agree.
steps.title: Verify before use

simulations.success: Sample labelled, cold-stored, logged without gaps, and verified.
simulations.safety_note: Training practice with fictional samples. Real lab work follows real protocols, real safety rules, and real oversight.

simulations.title: First Reading — Read Yourself
simulations.description: SIMULATION — practice the first reading: notice, name, check, choose. A practiced skill, not treatment.

steps.check: Something noticed and named plainly.
steps.instruction: Notice what is happening with you right now — body, mood, attention — without judging it.
steps.title: Notice

steps.check: Named in one plain sentence.
steps.instruction: Name it in plain words: what it is, not what it should be.
steps.title: Name it

steps.check: Checked; fits, or corrected.
steps.instruction: Check the reading against what you know: does it fit the facts of the day?
steps.title: Check it

steps.check: One response chosen with a reason.
steps.instruction: Choose one response — pause, ask, step back, or carry on — and say why.
steps.title: Choose a response

simulations.success: Noticed, named, checked, and a response chosen with a reason.
simulations.safety_note: Practice only. This is not therapy, not a diagnosis, and not a substitute for either.

simulations.title: Repair Circle
simulations.description: SIMULATION — repair something that broke between people, in the circle, in order.

steps.check: What happened is stated and heard.
steps.instruction: Acknowledge what happened, plainly, with everyone affected present.
steps.title: Acknowledge

steps.check: Each person heard; their words repeated back.
steps.instruction: Listen to how it landed — without defending, explaining, or correcting.
steps.title: Listen

steps.check: Repair named with an owner.
steps.instruction: Name the repair: what will be done differently, and by whom.
steps.title: Name the repair

steps.check: Next step agreed with a time to check.
steps.instruction: Agree what happens next and when you will check it held.
steps.title: Agree the next step

simulations.success: Acknowledged, listened, repair named with an owner, next step agreed.
simulations.safety_note: Practice only. Real conflict, harm, or safeguarding concerns need real people and real processes — not a simulation.

simulations.title: First Brief — Dashboard to Developer Desk
simulations.description: SIMULATION — run the First Brief quest as a desk exercise: dashboard, evidence, developer desk, in that order.

steps.check: Brief data collected; the site is named.
steps.instruction: At the Master Dashboard, collect the brief data for the site.
steps.title: Collect the brief data

steps.check: Each claim has a source — or is marked unchecked.
steps.instruction: Take the brief to the Evidence Layer and check its claims against sources.
steps.title: Check the evidence

steps.check: The desk has the brief and the evidence notes.
steps.instruction: Carry the checked brief to the Louisiana Developer Desk.
steps.title: Carry it to the Louisiana Developer Desk

steps.check: Gate questions answered from the brief, not from memory.
steps.instruction: Let the Level Gates test what the brief taught you.
steps.title: Test at the Academy

simulations.success: Brief collected, checked, delivered, and tested — in order.
simulations.safety_note: A training exercise. It is not investment advice, not a site assessment, and it makes no offer.

simulations.title: Evidence Review — Forecast vs Scout vs Review
simulations.description: SIMULATION — take one forecast claim through the three jobs: predict, find, check.

steps.check: One claim written down, dated.
steps.instruction: Collect the forecast spark at the Market Editions: one claim, with a date on it.
steps.title: Take the forecast

steps.check: At least one lead found, or the absence noted.
steps.instruction: Compare notes with the Scout Agent: what did the markets actually show?
steps.title: Scout for leads

steps.check: Each part of the claim is marked supported, contradicted, or unchecked.
steps.instruction: Bring the claim and the leads to the Review Agent and check them against the evidence.
steps.title: Check at the Evidence Layer

steps.check: Verdict written with its reasons.
steps.instruction: Write the verdict: what holds, what does not, and what is still missing.
steps.title: Give the verdict

simulations.success: A dated claim checked against evidence, with a written verdict.
simulations.safety_note: A training exercise in checking claims. It is not investment advice.

simulations.title: Supervised Tower-Crane Lift
simulations.description: SIMULATION — run a supervised tower-crane lift from plan to set-down, using the standard hand signals. Practice only; nothing here certifies anybody.

steps.check: One signal person named; everyone else knows to stay out of the signalling.
steps.instruction: Name one signal person for this lift. Only one person gives signals at a time.
steps.title: Designate the signal person

steps.check: Operator confirms each signal back.
steps.instruction: Confirm the standard signals with the operator: hoist, lower, raise/lower boom, swing, stop, emergency stop.
steps.title: Agree signals before the lift

steps.check: Chart says the lift is within limits; the decision is written on the lift plan.
steps.instruction: Read the chart posted in the bay: load, radius, boom angle. Decide go or no-go.
steps.title: Check the load chart

steps.check: Load is clear, steady, and holding.
steps.instruction: Signal HOIST: forearm vertical, index finger up, small circles. Raise the load clear of the ground and hold.
steps.title: Hoist the load

steps.check: Load is over the target; nobody is under it.
steps.instruction: Signal SWING: arm horizontal, index finger pointing in the direction of rotation.
steps.title: Swing to the target

steps.check: Load is set, stable, and the line is slack.
steps.instruction: Signal LOWER: arm and finger down, small circles. Set the load down and slack the line.
steps.title: Lower and set down

steps.check: The operator stopped immediately, from anyone's call.
steps.instruction: Anyone on the crew calls EMERGENCY STOP: both arms out, palms down, sweeping back and forth. The operator stops everything at once.
steps.title: Emergency-stop drill

simulations.success: All seven steps in order, including the emergency-stop drill.
simulations.safety_note: Simulation only. Real lifts need a qualified signal person, a real load chart for the actual crane, and site rules — none of which this room provides.

simulations.title: Rigging Signal Call
simulations.description: SIMULATION — the operator calls out a move; you give the matching standard signal. Five rounds, in order.

steps.check: Signal matches the move: hoist.
steps.instruction: The operator needs the load up. Give HOIST: forearm vertical, finger up, small circles.
steps.title: Round 1 — raise the load

steps.check: Signal matches the move: lower.
steps.instruction: The operator needs the load down. Give LOWER: arm and finger down, small circles.
steps.title: Round 2 — lower the load

steps.check: Signal matches the move: raise boom.
steps.instruction: The operator needs the boom up. Give RAISE BOOM: arm horizontal, fist closed, thumb up.
steps.title: Round 3 — raise the boom

steps.check: Signal matches the move: stop.
steps.instruction: The load is where it should be. Give STOP: one arm horizontal, palm down, back and forth.
steps.title: Round 4 — stop the movement

steps.check: Both arms, palms down; the operator stops everything.
steps.instruction: A hazard appears. Give EMERGENCY STOP: both arms out, palms down, back and forth — anyone may give it.
steps.title: Round 5 — emergency stop

simulations.success: All five signals matched first time, including the emergency stop.
simulations.safety_note: Drill only. The 19 standard signals are defined in OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart CC Appendix A; this drill covers five of them.

simulations.title: Load-Chart Judgment
simulations.description: SIMULATION — judge a lift from its chart. A no-go is a correct answer, not a failure.

steps.check: Load identified; nothing guessed.
steps.instruction: Find the load's weight and shape on the lift plan.
steps.title: Read the load

steps.check: Radius measured and written down.
steps.instruction: Measure the radius from the crane centre to the load's set-down point.
steps.title: Read the radius

steps.check: One row found; no other row used.
steps.instruction: Find the row for this boom length and radius on the chart posted in the bay.
steps.title: Find the chart row

steps.check: Decision made from the chart, with the reason stated.
steps.instruction: Compare the chart's limit with the load. Call GO or NO-GO and say why.
steps.title: Compare and decide

steps.check: Decision recorded and checked.
steps.instruction: Write the decision and the reason on the lift plan, and have the Operator Lead check it.
steps.title: Record the decision

simulations.success: A decision made from the chart and recorded — GO or NO-GO, with the reason.
simulations.safety_note: Judgment practice only. This room carries no real crane chart and no real load figures; a real lift needs the actual crane's chart and a qualified planner.
